Subject: Redwood discovery follow-up: Procurement & billing questions (next steps)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and a few asks to help us surface the right commercial path and get Procurement/Finance comfortable: 

1) Commercial path options: does Acme prefer to purchase via PO (purchase order + invoice) or via card/CC for this initial committed capacity? Any interest in marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace) down the line?

2) Billing / invoice requirements: Could you confirm the invoice requirements we should follow (billing address, legal entity, PO number placement on invoice, VAT/tax handling, and whether net-30 or net-45 terms are required)?

3) Procurement timelines & contacts: Who in Procurement will own the PO and contract review? If helpful, please share their preferred email and typical SLA for PO issuance after solution approval.

Attached is a quick invoice requirements checklist we use for enterprise customers — if you can fill or confirm the highlighted fields that will speed billing ops.

Next steps: once we have the procurement owner and invoice fields, I can loop in our Finance/Legal (Dev Patel) to prepare a customer-ready invoice and the standard order form. If PO is required, we’ll send a provisional invoice template that matches your format.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with Procurement if that helps.

Best,

Subject: Re: Redwood discovery follow-up: Procurement & billing questions (next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and checklist. Quick answers below: 

- Commercial path: Acme generally prefers PO for any multi-month commitments > $10k. For pilots under that threshold they will often use card. We are evaluating marketplace options but need internal approvals first.

- Billing / invoice requirements: Our billing needs are below (high level):
  * Legal entity: Acme Corporation, INC (EIN 12-3456789)
  * Billing address: 200 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105
  * VAT/Tax: US domestic — no VAT; sales tax not applicable for services at our enterprise entity.
  * PO number: must appear on invoice header and within the invoice PDF filename (e.g., PO-56789_invoice.pdf)
  * Payment terms: Net 45 preferred for new vendors, Net 30 acceptable for strategic partners; we'll confirm during contract stage.

I'll loop in Procurement (James) to confirm SLA for PO issuance. Attaching our billing ops intake email for reference.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product, Acme Corp
olivia@acme-corp.com

Attachment: acme_internal_billing_guidelines.pdf (sent by procurement)

From: James Park <james.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Moss <olivia@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood discovery follow-up: Procurement & billing questions (next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the note. A few procurement specifics: 

- PO process: Our standard procurement flow is: SOW/Order Form review (legal), internal approvals (2–3 business days), PO generation (1–2 business days once approved). Overall typical lead time ~5 business days from final order form.

- Approver & contact: procurement@acme-corp.com is monitored; I'm the primary contact for vendor onboarding (james.park@acme-corp.com).

- Invoice format: We require a PDF invoice with: invoice number, invoice date, PO number on header, line-item breakdown (monthly rate, seats, tax), and bank wiring instructions when applicable. We can accept emailed invoices to ap@acme-corp.com or an SFTP drop; our preference is emailed PDF with PO in filename.

- Payment terms: We typically request Net 45 for new vendors; Net 30 available after vendor undergoes onboarding and references.

- Tax/VAT: Not applicable for US domestic entity. If Redwood issues from a foreign legal entity we will need a W-8/W-9 as applicable.

If you can provide a draft invoice template and a proposed order form, we can fast-track the internal approvals.

—James
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
james.park@acme-corp.com
